solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Station with loveliest porter working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a new order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A railway porter at some station is singled out as the loveliest one on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' is the anagram signal on LOVELIEST PORTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A major London railway terminus serving East Anglia, so it is an example of a station.

clue.text: Bankers' reading is restricted by unacceptable service of Labour

indicators.note: restricted by says the reading matter and is are hemmed in by the service word

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that must be replayed
the FT, the Financial Times, is the newspaper bankers read

explanation.surface: A grumble that the bankers' paper is limited by the poor service of the Labour government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is the tennis serve, not public service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour Party is on the political left, so a supporter's views lean towards socialism.

clue.text: Grand house around a northern plain

indicators.note: around says the house word goes about the following letters

parts.note: a villa is a large country house

explanation.surface: A stately mansion on a flat expanse in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like a noun for flat country; it is the adjective meaning ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and unembellished, like the default ice-cream flavour, so ordinary and unadorned.

clue.text: Waste time as mouse did at 13:00

definitions.meaning: to use up the remaining time deliberately, as a leading team does at the end of a match
in the nursery rhyme Hickory Dickory Dock the mouse ran back down when the clock struck one, and 13:00 is one o'clock

explanation.surface: Time-wasting compared with the mouse of the nursery rhyme at one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports phrase for wasting time while ahead, and literally what the rhyme's mouse did.

clue.text: Views confusion in what one knows well

indicators.note: in says the confusion word goes inside the other word

parts.note: to know one's onions is to know a subject well
pi or pie is printers' type mixed up in confusion

explanation.surface: Muddled views about a subject one knows thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what one knows well' points at the idiom 'know one's onions', an everyday British phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Beliefs or judgements a person holds are their views on a matter.

clue.text: Like a music maker some highly rated

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some music makers are highly rated, a comparison of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like a lyre, an ancient stringed instrument, so resembling a maker of music.

clue.text: In which some flee Nazis and find custom house disturbing

indicators.note: disturbing means thrown out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refugees escaping Nazis find the customs post at the border unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' is the anagram signal on FIND CUSTOM HOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical film ends with the von Trapp family escaping the Nazis over the mountains.

clue.text: Very religious French priest following English one enjoying good things

indicators.note: following places the religious and priest words after the English letter

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very religious
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A devout French priest succeeds an English one who loves life's pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is old schoolboy slang for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes refined pleasure in fine food and drink savours the good things of life.

clue.text: Aquatic creature's driven one from river not stable

indicators.note: driven, with from, says the creature has pushed the one out of the river and taken its place

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river
A is one
an otter is an aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: A water animal has chased something away from the river, which is unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is Scotland's longest river. 'one' is A, the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and wobbly, as an unsteady walker, so lacking stability.

clue.text: 'Gnome' more decorative outside home

indicators.note: outside says the word for more decorative goes round the word for home

parts.note: fancier means more ornate or decorative
in means at home

explanation.surface: A garden gnome is said to look more decorative when placed outside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'gnomes of Zurich' was a jibe at Swiss bankers, so the quoted 'Gnome' is a money man, not a garden ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'gnomes of Zurich' were the Swiss bankers and money dealers, so a gnome here is a person who manages money.

clue.text: Order English book you may need shortly

parts.note: a dictionary is the book a solver may need, and shortly cuts it to its abbreviation dict

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy an English textbook that a student will need soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' reads as 'soon' but asks for the short form DICT of dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree or official command is an order issued by an authority.

clue.text: Simple dwelling has one grand facility

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
G is short for grand, a thousand
facility is a euphemism for a lavatory, the loo

explanation.surface: A modest home boasts a single impressive amenity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility' is the toilet, loo in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow house is a basic shelter, a plain kind of home.

clue.text: Bring in drastic reduction

indicators.note: drastic suggests severe upheaval, so the letters of the next word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A call to bring in a severe cut, as in budgets or prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drastic' is the anagram signal on REDUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: To present or bring in something new, such as a law or a person, is a synonym.

clue.text: Getting fit, sound as a bell, accepting bad weather

indicators.note: accepting says the sound takes the weather word inside it

parts.note: ting is the light ringing sound a bell makes
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: Someone working out, feeling perfectly healthy, puts up with the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy; here it is the noise a bell makes, TING.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising to improve fitness is what an athlete does in preparation, so the gerund matches.

clue.text: Dwarf seen messing about with two axes

indicators.note: messing about means being rearranged carelessly, so the letters of seen are jumbled

parts.note: z and y are two of the axes used in graphs and geometry

explanation.surface: A dwarf has been spotted playing around with a pair of axes, perhaps in the mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' means chopping tools in the surface but graph axes, Z and Y, in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the seven dwarfs in the Disney Snow White film, so it is an example of a dwarf.

clue.text: Shrub appeared sickly coming up on middle of heath

parts.note: came means arrived or appeared

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue says the word for sickly is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ill means sickly

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letter of the word heath

explanation.surface: A shrub on a heath looked unwell as it grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns ILL into LLI.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen flowering bush related to the tea plant, so an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Dance 'Tea for Two'

indicators.note: Two asks for the tea word to appear twice in a row

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A dance performed to the old song 'Tea for Two'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea for Two' is a well-known song title, but here it means CHA written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom routine with a quick triple step, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Top soldier engages girl in great work

indicators.note: engages says the soldier holds the girl within

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief, the top soldier
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A general hires a young woman for a major work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engages' reads as employs; here it means takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of lasting excellence, such as a canonical novel, is a masterpiece.

clue.text: Plant up to now mostly found in Lincoln

indicators.note: found in says the shortened word sits inside the name

parts.note: Abe is the short name of Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: still means up to now, as before

explanation.surface: A plant that has been found growing in Lincoln until now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' looks like the English city but is Abe Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: A perennial garden flower with feathery plumes, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: See flush in nasty chap, drunk

indicators.note: in says the flush word sits inside the nasty chap

parts.note: a cad is an ungentlemanly, nasty man
to flush game is to rouse it from cover, startling it into flight

explanation.surface: Look at the red face of an unpleasant man who has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' suggests a reddened face, but it is the hunting sense: startle from cover. 'See' only directs the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink heavily and noisily, so the past form matches having drunk freely.

clue.text: What's upset you and me keeping endangered species in prison

indicators.note: keeping says the reversed pronoun holds the animal
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: us means you and me
the giant panda is a famous endangered species

explanation.surface: Someone asks what has bothered us about holding a rare animal in captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' means distressed in the surface but turns US into SU.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berlin jail where Nazi war criminals including Rudolf Hess were held.

clue.text: American lawyer compiled state information

parts.note: DA is a US district attorney

indicators.note: compiled means put together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A US attorney gathers official information about a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiled' is the anagram signal on STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of facts or records gathered together is a body of information.

clue.text: Change of government on the ticket

parts.note: a coup is an overthrow of government

explanation.surface: A political change appears on the ballot ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticket' looks like the electoral slate; it is a voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher or slip to exchange for goods or a discount is a ticket.

clue.text: Take choir performing what may come after 'Jerusalem'

indicators.note: performing suggests the words are put through their paces, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A choir is told to sing the next item after the hymn 'Jerusalem'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerusalem' looks like Blake's hymn, but the definition wants the vegetable name that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerusalem artichoke is a knobbly root vegetable, so the word follows Jerusalem in its name.

clue.text: A felon finally caught by London police on purpose

indicators.note: caught by says the A and letter are held inside the police word

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police of London

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word felon

explanation.surface: A criminal is at last arrested by the London police, and deliberately so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like 'at last' for the arrest; it takes N, the end of 'felon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done intentionally is intended, deliberate rather than accidental.

clue.text: A lot of shots heal almost nothing

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the healing word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to salve is to soothe or heal
O is the round zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: Lots of injections hardly cure anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shots' could mean injections; here it means gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A simultaneous discharge of many guns is a volley, a great many shots at once.

clue.text: Illicit sales paid fences

indicators.note: illicit suggests something improper, so the words are reworked into an irregular order

explanation.surface: Receivers of stolen goods, fences, are paid through illegal sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fences' looks like the criminal dealers suggested by the surface; it means stake barriers.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of pointed wooden stakes forming a defensive barrier is a fence, so the plural works.

clue.text: Corroborating evidence where Americans hold money

definitions.meaning: verifying a version of events, testing a story against facts
the US name for a current bank account from which cheques are drawn

explanation.surface: Checking evidence and checking a US bank balance.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage this is a current account; separately it reads as verifying a report.
